Commentary.Commentary: Welcome back for the chase. Kyle Mayers and Brandon King will open for West Indies. It will be Sam Curran to start with the ball for England. Here we go!
... RUN CHASE ...

Andre Russell is up for a quick chat and expresses joy at being back after a couple of years of absence. He commends England for a strong start and reveals ongoing team discussions about limiting them to 170-180, a goal they achieve. Looking ahead, he remains optimistic about the chase, expressing hope for successfully reaching the target. He highlights the grippy wicket, advocating for pace variations. Mentions that aiming for a 50, not 70, in the powerplay for a robust start. Emphasizing the team's deep batting, he sees it as crucial for laying a strong foundation.

The Windies bowlers got a hammering early on but they came back strongly. Andre Russell was the best bowler on show with 3 for 19 in his spell. Romario Shepherd chipped in with 2 while Akeal Hosein and Jason Holder got one each. Joseph picked up three wickets as well but was on the expensive side. Right then, the bowlers have done the job and it's up to the West Indies batting unit to chase this and get an early lead. Can they do it? We shall find out. Join us in a bit for the second essay.

What a turnaround this has been from the West Indies. England were going brilliantly at 112 for 2 at the halfway mark and the hosts have come back strongly to dismiss them for 171 inside the 20 overs. Batting first, England got off to an excellent start with Salt and Buttler adding 77 for the first wicket in just over six overs. Salt departed but Buttler kept going and kept the tempo. Jacks, Livingstone, and Ben Duckett, all got starts but none of them carried on and stayed till the close of the innings. The pitch is getting slow and the chase will not be an easy one.

OUT! An excellent review from West Indies and credit to Nicholas Pooran. On a length going over the off-pole, Tymal Mills looks to play it toward the on side but misses out as the keeper collects it. Nicholas Pooran asks the skipper for a review for Caught-behind and Rovman Powell asks for it. There is a clear spike as the ball is next to the bat and the umpire is asked to reverse his decision to OUT. West Indies bundle out England inside 20 over at 171.

Commentary.Commentary: We are ready for the live-action as the umpires make their way into the middle followed by the players of the West Indies who spread out to the respective field positions. Jos Buttler and Phil Salt are the two openers while Akeal Hosein will bowl the first over.

Skipper of England Jos Buttler says that they were looking to bowl first as well. Adds that he is looking forward to the series and says that they will do some experimentation in the lead-up to the T20 World Cup. Mentions that both Rehan Ahmed and Adil Rashid are playing today and that he will open the batting. Ends by sharing that he is hoping for an exciting game.

Skipper of West Indies Rovman Powell has opted to bowl first. He says considering the favorable surface they will aim to restrict the opponents to a low total. Mentions that with 6 specialist batters, along with the all-rounders, a spinner, and the premier pacer Alzarri Joseph, they are geared up. Adds that this series holds significant importance with the World Cup looming in 6 months, offering a valuable opportunity to assess the side.
England (Playing XI) - Jos Buttler (C)(WK), Phil Salt, Will Jacks, Ben Duckett, Harry Brook, Liam Livingstone, Sam Curran, Chris Woakes, Rehan Ahmed, Adil Rashid, Tymal Mills
West Indies (Playing XI) - Brandon King, Kyle Mayers, Shai Hope, Nicholas Pooran (WK), Shimron Hetmyer, Rovman Powell (C), Romario Shepherd, Andre Russell, Jason Holder, Akeal Hosein, Alzarri Joseph.
TOSS - West Indies have won the toss and they have decided to Field first.

This series also marks the use of Stop Clock trial rule. In simple words, this is an attempt to close out the game in the span of three and a half hours. In Stop Clock trial rule, a stop clock will begin as soon as the over finishes and the fielding side will have to be ready to start the next over within 60 seconds. The umpires will give them two warnings initially and on breaching the third, the fielding side will be penalized with 5 runs. This rule will definitely add some spice in the contest and teams will have to adapt quickly. The series promises to be an exciting one. So, sit back and enjoy all the action. Toss and team news coming up shortly. Stay tuned!

England, on the other hand, carried on their dismal form from the recently concluded World Cup and lost another ODI series. A lot of their first-choice players were not on this tour but they have enough quality to beat any side on their given day. England have called up the experienced trio of Moeen Ali, Adil Rashid, and Chris Woakes into the squad while the left-arm quick Tymal Mills also makes his way back in the English colours. England will want to forget the ODI series and start on a fresh note in the T20Is.

Hello and a warm welcome to our coverage of the 1st T20I in this 5-match series between England and West Indies from the Kensington Oval in Barbados. The hosts, West Indies are coming off a brilliant series win by a margin of 2-1 in the ODI leg of the tour and will hope to carry on the momentum in the T20s as well. The Windies have added to fresh faces to the squad with Rovman Powell returning to lead the side while the T20 specialists in Nicholas Pooran, Andre Russell, and Jason Holder also forming the part of this squad. West Indies will be hosting the T20 World Cup in close to six months’ time and this series gives them a good opportunity to build their squad in the lead up to the mega event.
…MATCHDAY…

After an enthralling three-match ODI series, it is now time for a five-match T20I series between hosts West Indies and England. The 1st T20I of the series will be played at the Kensington Oval in Bridgetown, Barbados which was also the venue of the third and final ODI. With the series locked in at 1-1, the rain gods decided to show up and the hosts managed to pull off a remarkable four-wicket win to seal their first bilateral series win against a full-member nation in a long while and their first against England in more than 15 years. With that said, the 2024 T20 World Cup is about six months away and with the tournament taking place in the Caribbean alongside the United States, this series will prove to be a good dress rehearsal for the main event. England are the reigning T20 World Champions but have been battered and bruised in the last few months. They will look to get back to their best with some no-fear cricket. West Indies on the other hand were the T20 powerhouse in the 2010s but in the last few years, their golden generation of T20 cricketers has retired and the void hasn't been filled yet. They do have players like Nicholas Pooran, Rovman Powell and even Andre Russell who are coming off some positive performances in franchise cricket and will look to translate the same form here. Can the reigning World Champions regain their mojo and start with a win? Or will the Windies notch up another famous win? We shall find out.
